prompt: A user wants to send data to one recipient rather than every member. Which term applies?
options: Unicast
Broadcast
Offline replication
Multicast to all groups
explanation: Unicast addresses one destination; broadcast and multicast have different audience scopes. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 12.

prompt: Two waveforms differ in supported services and protection. What should selection be based on?
options: Required compatibility, services and approved security needs
Only whether one waveform appears first in a menu
Only the shortest waveform name
The assumption that all listed waveforms are interchangeable
explanation: The source lists distinct waveform capabilities; planning must compare requirements rather than equate labels. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, pages 31, 34, 35, 36.

prompt: Inspection reveals a damaged cable and bent connector pins. What is justified?
options: Assume a software reset repairs the physical damage
Record the fault and follow authorized maintenance procedures
Force the connector until the fault disappears
Ignore the issue if the display still lights up
explanation: Physical defects require appropriate maintenance; power-on alone does not demonstrate equipment integrity. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 25.

prompt: A performance test sends 100 packets and records 90 received. What does this directly show?
options: Ten packets were not received during that test
Every voice conversation will fail at the same rate
The fault has been proven to be a broken antenna
The entire network is permanently unusable
explanation: The counts describe that test's outcome; they do not alone establish permanence, application effects or root cause. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 67.

prompt: A legacy voice call succeeds but position updates do not reach the application. What remains to verify?
options: Whether working voice proves the data must already be present
Whether the application can be ignored because radios transmit
The data service and its integration path
Only the voice handset's volume setting
explanation: Voice success is not evidence that data interfaces, routing and receiving applications work correctly. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, pages 69, 72, 73.

prompt: After a link changes, the MANET finds another path. The shared picture still shows yesterday's reports. What should the team distinguish?
options: A display's color scheme from the radio's procurement date
Restored connectivity from the freshness of received reports
Successful rerouting from a complete loss of all communication
A new path from proof that the reports are factually accurate
explanation: Self-healing concerns connectivity adaptation. A useful shared picture also depends on appropriate information, so rerouting does not demonstrate freshness. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 12; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 9.

prompt: Management traffic uses authenticated, confidential SNMPv3 communication. An application user nevertheless has permissions beyond assigned duties. Which conclusion fits?
options: Application permissions can be assessed from the radio model alone
The permission issue proves that SNMPv3 has no protection function
Protected management traffic does not settle application authorization
The management protocol establishes the user's complete access rights
explanation: SNMPv3 protection applies to management traffic. Authentication, authorization and other controls remain necessary in the integrated information system. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 30; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 24.

prompt: A training link becomes intermittent after equipment is moved outdoors. The team notices a damaged cable and also suspects environmental effects. Which approach is best supported?
options: Diagnose outdoor propagation from the previously successful indoor test
Replace the radio with a higher-capacity set to offset the observed packet interruptions
Inspect the visible condition and assess relevant environmental evidence
Adjust service priorities to restore the traffic pattern seen in the earlier indoor trial
explanation: The sources support physical-condition checks and consideration of environmental constraints. Neither a suspected cause nor an earlier successful test is a complete diagnosis. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 25; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 18.

prompt: RX/TX diagnostics run, but the team has recorded only version information. The users report missing updates. Which evidence is still needed?
options: Observed performance of the required report-delivery path
A second copy of the recorded software version number
A list of command appointments from the organization chart
A statement that the diagnostic menu was successfully opened
explanation: The diagnostics include path and performance information. The C2 feedback requirement concerns updates reaching decision-makers, so menu access and version records alone are insufficient. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 58; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 25.

prompt: A proposed gateway forwards every available report between two classroom networks, although only one approved report type is required. What should be clarified?
options: The equipment labels before deciding who may handle information
The gateway's appearance before reviewing traffic leakage concerns
Required exchange and boundary rules before widening traffic
The display size before documenting the required exchange
explanation: The integrator's traffic-limiting role and the ICD's exchange rules support defining necessary flows. Broad forwarding is not justified merely by technical capability. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 70; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 16.

prompt: Sensors collect useful observations, but no decision-maker receives them. What is the central shortfall?
options: The information path is not effectively integrated
The presence of sensors already satisfies the requirement
The sensors necessarily failed to detect anything
The organization needs fewer information users
explanation: Collection alone does not deliver usable situational awareness; information must reach its intended users. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, pages 7, 9.

prompt: A disaster-response exercise needs remote aerial mapping. Which listed platform fits that role?
options: UAS
Fixed network router
Telephone exchange
SUGV
explanation: UAS can carry sensors for remote sensing and mapping; the role stated is aerial. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 10.

prompt: A team proposes commercial phones for protected information. Which requirement governs whether that proposed use is permitted?
options: Service contracts and staff training
Applicable COMSEC and authorized-use requirements
Vendor assurance and procurement approval
Approved encryption and device inventory
explanation: Special-purpose commercial communications are governed by policy; convenience is not sufficient authorization. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 17.

prompt: A new sensor fails to work with an older receiving system. Which constraint is illustrated?
options: Public advertising reach
Legacy compatibility
Document classification alone
Personnel seniority
explanation: Legacy integration requires compatibility work rather than assuming newer and older equipment will interoperate. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 18.

prompt: An upgrade replaces one module. What should be rechecked?
options: Only whether the old module can still be photographed
Only the replacement's packaging color
Whether modular design removes every test requirement
Compatibility and relevant end-to-end behavior
explanation: Modularity eases replacement; it does not prove that the changed system still meets its requirements. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 29.

prompt: A sensor vendor demonstrates reliable observation delivery and says the automated output also assigns decision authority. What should the review separate?
options: The supplier's technical demonstration from the equipment purchase cost
Collection and delivery capability from assigned organizational authority
The display's physical size from the number of operator accounts
A sensor's observation role from whether computers can store data
explanation: A sensor detects and collects; technical delivery does not confer command responsibility. Authority must come from the organization's assigned roles. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 7; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 7.

prompt: An exercise report combines one directional measurement with a map icon labeled exact position. What is the strongest immediate correction?
options: Preserve the measurement's uncertainty when interpreting and displaying it
Remove the report's source information to make the display easier to read
Accept the precise icon because all participants see the same map
Treat delivery to several users as independent confirmation of position
explanation: A bearing alone does not establish an exact position. Interpretation and presentation should not give the observation greater certainty than its evidence supports. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 10; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slides 10, 11, 13.

prompt: Two participating networks have different internal designs but agree on their exchange boundary. Which assessment is appropriate?
options: Assess the internal equipment inventory as the basis for accepting the shared interface
Accept the interface using each network's previous test record
Compare nominal network capacity as the basis for accepting the information exchange
Evaluate the defined connection points and required information exchange
explanation: IOPs standardize connections while permitting internal differences. The review should assess the defined interfaces and actual exchange requirements. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 16; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 17.

prompt: A classroom network carries all collected reports, yet operators miss important updates among the volume. Which response addresses both lessons?
options: Replace the analysis requirement with a higher received-strength reading
Judge success solely by whether every source remains connected
Review traffic priorities together with operator processing needs
Increase stored report volume while retaining the same review process
explanation: QoS addresses competing network demand, while sensor integration also faces information overload. Both transport and the users' ability to process relevant information matter. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 18; MANET C4ISTAR Planning, pages 9, 12.

prompt: A design adds a backup component and declares the complete integrated system secure. What must the review still examine?
options: The number of years since the system concept was first presented
Whether both components appear in the same purchase request
Whether the drawing shows the backup in a different color
Other CIA controls and whether the required service survives failure
explanation: Redundancy reduces a particular dependency; it does not establish complete security. Availability behavior and other confidentiality/integrity controls still require evidence. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 29; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 24.

prompt: A design includes radios and computers but no people or procedures. What is missing from the source's C2 concept?
options: Its diagnostic coverage and maintenance configuration
Its organizational and human components
Its encryption and identity-verification capabilities
Its approved technical interface and message-format profile
explanation: The C2 system includes people and processes, not just technical nodes. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slides 7, 14.

prompt: A user can technically open a system and assumes that grants decision authority. What distinction matters?
options: The ability to read data authorizes every subsequent action
A successful login assigns every command responsibility
Technical access and command authority are different
Network availability overrides all assigned roles
explanation: Access permissions and institutional decision authority are separate concepts. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slides 7, 24.

prompt: Devices exchange data, but staff use incompatible procedures and terminology. What still needs attention?
options: Nothing beyond successful packet transfer
Human and procedural interoperability
Only the equipment purchase dates
Only the physical cable connectors
explanation: The lesson's interoperability scope includes people and processes as well as technical exchange. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 18.

prompt: Both applications use TCP/IP but disagree on message meaning. What remains unresolved?
options: The existence of their network interfaces
Application-level interoperability
The spelling of the protocol name
Whether both can use a network protocol
explanation: Common transport does not guarantee agreement on the meaning and format of application information. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 23.

prompt: A history review describes mobile command centers as part of capability development. What conceptual need do they address?
options: Communications and C2 support beyond a fixed headquarters
A replacement for all trained staff and procedures
Automatic authority independent of the chain of command
Unlimited connectivity without supporting infrastructure
explanation: The historical discussion treats mobility as extending C2 support, not removing its organizational and technical dependencies. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slides 30, 31.

prompt: Messages cross an agreed interface, but operators apply incompatible meanings to one status field. Which gap is most directly shown?
options: A lack of any stored information on either computer
A failure to purchase identical equipment for both teams
A complete absence of any functioning communication path
Shared interpretation and procedures beyond successful transport
explanation: Technical exchange is only part of interoperability. Teams must also share the information's intended interpretation and applicable procedures. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 18; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 16.

prompt: An integrator makes a report technically accessible to a second system. The user asks whether access approval is now unnecessary. Which answer fits?
options: The integrator's connection replaces every recipient authorization check
The sender's radio model determines the recipient's need for access
The receiving display's successful login settles the report's release
The exchange path still requires the applicable access safeguards
explanation: An integrator enables exchanges; it does not remove authentication, authorization and other safeguards required by the integrated system. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 24; MANET C4ISTAR Planning, pages 69, 70.

prompt: A replacement component has the same physical connector as the old one. Its message format changed. What is needed before claiming compatibility?
options: Verify connector fit and transport delivery using the previous message format
Review the replacement's generic certificate against the existing profile
Repeat the old component's acceptance test using its established interpretation criteria
Review the exchange specification and test the replacement's interpretation
explanation: An ICD defines exchange rules, and modular upgrades must preserve compatibility. Physical fit alone does not establish compatible message meaning. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 20; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 29.

prompt: A TCP/IP connection transfers a file between two training systems. The acceptance requirement also includes voice coordination. Which statement is justified?
options: The file-transfer result proves every receiver has the same permissions
The voice requirement is irrelevant once application data can move
The file-transfer result does not demonstrate the separate voice requirement
The shared transport standard completes every required service test
explanation: The lessons distinguish network communication from application/service requirements. Each required service needs relevant evidence. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 23; MANET C4ISTAR Planning, pages 69, 72, 73.

prompt: A project lists communications and sensor equipment but no ownership of maintenance or information handoffs. Which addition best strengthens the architecture?
options: A longer equipment inventory without assigning responsibilities
A single hardware diagram used in place of an operating process
A rule letting the first available user settle every interface decision
Named responsibilities and coordinated processes for the two capability areas
explanation: The architecture relates actors and processes to information. The complementary C4 and sensor responsibilities need explicit coordination rather than equipment-only planning. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 29; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 27.
